text: Two things to start, and four numbers to finish the picture. Type them straight into the clipboard.
bullets: To start: one name to own this, and who in IT gives read access.
The four numbers turn the cost into a difference and size both desks on your real hours.
At the end of step 2 you have your own dead bed time. If it is smaller than we said, you will know first.
chat.invite: Send what you have. Rough answers are fine.
prompts: Who else should see this plan?
chat.pointer: Type on each line of the clipboard. Every line you fill is added to your message.

blocks.title: What we need from you
blocks.deck: Six lines on a clipboard. Each one you fill goes into your message.

blocks.title: What we need to start
blocks.sub: Rough answers are fine. Leave a line empty if you do not know yet.

asks.title: Who in IT gives read access

have: What a bed earns a day

sheets.title: One name to own this
sheets.text: Someone has to own the plan until the managers join. It can be a person you already have.

sheets.title: Who in IT gives read access
sheets.text: Read access to admissions, discharges, billing and the bed board. Nothing is changed in your systems.

sheets.title: Desk roster on each shift
sheets.text: Turns the cost from a total into a difference. Today we count every seat as new.

sheets.title: When patients arrive, by hour
sheets.text: Checks the three Admissions Executives against your real busiest hour.

sheets.title: Bed moves inside the hospital
sheets.text: The desk also handles moves between wards. They count in the busiest hour.

sheets.title: When discharges happen
sheets.text: Sizes the discharge desk. The usual rule may give too many, so we wait for your times.

blocks.label: After step 2
blocks.sub: Measured, not guessed. If it is smaller than we said, you know before spending anything on people or process.

add.detail: Add something else we should know

jump.detail: Back to what is really wrong
